name: Ringan no Olo
subtitle: fire-roasted aubergine mashed with raw garlic and green chilli, smoky and fierce

ingredients.note: the fat purple globe kind, not slim ones

ingredients.qty: 12 cloves, crushed to a coarse paste
ingredients.note: olo is a garlic dish; do not cut this back
generous oil is what makes it olo and not bharta
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free

prepNotes: Rub the whole aubergines with a little oil and slit each one twice so steam escapes. Otherwise they burst on the flame.
Roast directly on a gas flame if you have one. That char is the entire flavour of the dish and an oven does not give it.
Half the garlic goes in raw at the end. Crush it to a paste rather than chopping so it disappears into the mash.

steps.text: Set the aubergines straight on a medium gas flame, turning every couple of minutes, 12-15 minutes in all, until the skin is blistered black all over and the flesh has collapsed.
steps.tip: Push a knife into the thickest part. If there is any resistance, keep roasting. Undercooked olo tastes bitter.

steps.text: Rest them in a covered bowl 5 minutes, then peel off the charred skin and mash the flesh coarsely with a fork. Leave some texture.
Heat the oil in a kadhai, crackle the cumin, add the asafoetida and half the crushed garlic and fry 30 seconds until it smells sweet, not brown.
Add the onion and cook over medium heat until soft and pale gold, about 6 minutes.
Stir in half the green chilli, the turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder, then the tomato. Cook 6-7 minutes until the tomato breaks down and the oil separates at the edges.
steps.tip: Wait for the oil to separate. That is the point at which the masala stops tasting of raw spice.

steps.text: Fold in the mashed aubergine and salt. Cook uncovered 8 minutes, mashing against the side of the pan, until it thickens and darkens.
Take it off the heat and stir through the remaining raw crushed garlic, the remaining green chilli and the lemon juice.
steps.tip: The raw garlic at the end is what makes it Kathiawadi. Add it off the heat so it stays sharp.

steps.text: Rest 5 minutes, stir in the coriander and serve with hot bajra rotlo and a spoon of butter or a raw onion.

storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated and the smoke deepens overnight. Reheat in a pan with a teaspoon of oil; do not add water, it goes watery and flat.

nutrition.method: Estimated from raw ingredients using USDA FoodData Central. Cooking losses are not modelled and added salt is excluded, so sodium is not given.
